newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIAN BROADCASTING CORP MORNING UPDATE.

text.p: NEW HIGH COURT JUDGE
The Federal Government has recommended to the Governor-General that Justice Kenneth Hayne be appointed to the High Court.

Attorney-General, Daryl Williams, said 52-year-old Justice Hayne who is currently a judge of the Supreme Court of Victoria. He would replace Sir Daryl Dawson who retires from the High Court at the end of the week.
The appointment has been welcomed in legal circles and the judge is expected to take up the position at the end of the month.
Constitutional law expert, Cheryl Saunders, said it is not possible to say whether it is a conservative appointment.
CAR PROVIDES FRESH LEAD IN WHELAN DISAPPEARANCE
A four-wheel drive vehicle believed to be linked to the disappearance of Sydney woman Kerry Whelan has been found by police.
Detectives from Operation Bellaire said they had tracked down the silver-blue Suzuki Vitara in a Sydney suburb.
It will undergo a scientific examination this morning.
Mrs Whelan was last seen parking her car at a Parramatta car park on May 6.
Detectives investigating the case said the discovery of the vehicle was a possible breakthrough.
REPORT GIVES AUSTRALIANS A HEALTHY DIAGNOSIS
The health of Australians is improving but there are still some worrying trends, according to a new report.
The document is the first since federal, state and territory ministers began a new data collection program to help tackle health issues.
The report on five national health priority areas has found cardiovascular disease is still the biggest killer of Australians, but fewer people are dying from it.
It said too many Australians are still at risk of developing the disease through factors such as smoking and obesity.
One of the report's main concerns is a rise in the suicide rate for 15 to 34-year-old men, in contrast to the overall trend.
Other findings include an increase in the number of new cases of cancer diagnosed - a situation attributed to better detection methods - and a growing and ageing population.
COALITION MPS HAVE A WIN ON MEDIA LAW CHANGES
The Federal Coalition's backbench has had a win with Cabinet deferring any decision on changes to media ownership rules until Coalition MPs are consulted.
The Communications Minister, Richard Alston, took a proposal to Cabinet for relaxing cross-media ownership laws, with a new media regulator to hold a public inquiry.
Media proprietors would have to argue their cases publicly, before final approval would be given to any changes in ownership.
The Coalition Communications Committee wrote to the Prime Minister seeking his assurance that the backbench would be consulted before Cabinet finalised its position.
A Government source said Cabinet discussed media ownership laws and decided to hold further consultations with the backbench.
